reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Scriver's OMMBID
clinicalPearls: Represents the mildest (attenuated) end of the mucopolysaccharidosis type I spectrum, caused by partial deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme alpha-L-iduronidase
Intelligence is characteristically preserved, distinguishing it clinically from severe Hurler syndrome at the opposite end of the same enzymatic disorder
Presentation is often delayed into later childhood or adulthood with corneal clouding, joint stiffness, and carpal tunnel syndrome
Aortic valve disease, particularly regurgitation, is a recognised cardiac manifestation
Stature is usually normal or only mildly reduced, contrasting with the marked growth failure of Hurler syndrome
Diagnosis rests on demonstrating reduced alpha-L-iduronidase activity together with raised urinary dermatan and heparan sulfate
Molecular confirmation of IDUA gene variants clarifies the phenotype and supports genetic counselling
reference.pathophysiology: Scheie syndrome arises from biallelic pathogenic variants in the IDUA gene, which encodes the lysosomal hydrolase alpha-L-iduronidase. Residual enzyme activity is greater than in Hurler syndrome, producing a milder phenotype within the same disease continuum. Impaired breakdown of the glycosaminoglycans dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate leads to their progressive accumulation within lysosomes of connective tissue, cornea, cartilage, heart valves, and other organs. The stored substrate is also excreted in excess in the urine. Because intellectual function is generally spared, the clinical burden is dominated by musculoskeletal, ocular, and cardiac involvement that worsens slowly over years. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Hurler and Hurler-Scheie syndromes (other points on the MPS I spectrum)
Rheumatoid or juvenile idiopathic arthritis given the joint stiffness
Mucolipidoses with overlapping skeletal and connective tissue features
Other causes of corneal clouding such as cystinosis or Fabry disease
additionalInvestigations: Leucocyte or fibroblast alpha-L-iduronidase enzyme assay
Quantitative urinary glycosaminoglycan analysis with electrophoresis for dermatan and heparan sulfate
IDUA gene sequencing for molecular confirmation and genotype-phenotype correlation
Slit-lamp examination to document corneal clouding
Echocardiography to assess aortic and mitral valve function
Nerve conduction studies where carpal tunnel syndrome is suspected
redFlags: Progressive aortic valve regurgitation or other cardiac valve dysfunction
Visual deterioration from advancing corneal clouding
Median nerve compression causing hand weakness and wasting
Cervical spine or airway compromise from connective tissue deposition
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy can approach normal in many patients, though progressive cardiac valve disease, corneal clouding, and joint limitation cause substantial long-term morbidity. Enzyme replacement therapy may help systemic manifestations but does not correct established corneal or valvular changes.
pitfalls: Attributing joint stiffness to inflammatory arthritis and missing the underlying storage disorder
Assuming preserved intellect excludes a mucopolysaccharidosis
Overlooking silent valvular heart disease that requires surveillance
Delaying enzyme replacement therapy because early features are subtle
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Offer enzyme replacement therapy with laronidase (recombinant alpha-L-iduronidase) as the mainstay to reduce glycosaminoglycan storage and systemic burden
Refer for surgical carpal tunnel decompression and provide physiotherapy for joint stiffness and contractures
Manage progressive aortic valve disease with cardiology surveillance and valve surgery when indicated
Arrange corneal transplantation for visually significant corneal clouding, which enzyme therapy does not reverse
Monitor with serial echocardiography, slit-lamp examination, nerve conduction studies, and screening for sleep-disordered breathing
Coordinate multidisciplinary care and offer genetic counselling for the autosomal recessive inheritance and family screening
